# name: # format: ttl, nt, trig, nq, or rdf (RDF/XML, converted to N-Triples by the harness);
# nq-head: the first megabytes of a gzipped N-Quads dump, cut at the last full line;
# sparql-examples: a tarball of the SIB sparql-examples repository, unpacked into
# NAME/; every sh:select / sh:ask / sh:construct / sh:describe / sh:update in
# its .ttl files is a SPARQL case.
# sha256: the hash fetch.sh checks after it stores a file (and for files already
# present on every run). A change prints a warning and keeps the file; with
# CORPUS_STRICT=1 it fails the run. It covers the file as stored in test/corpus/:
# for nq-head the cut file, not the gzip range; for sparql-examples a tree hash
# (the sha256 of `sha256sum`-style lines, "HASH  ./path", for every file under
# the unpacked directory, sorted by path in the C locale). Empty means unchecked.
# Update one with: tools/corpus/fetch.sh -f, then copy the hash from the warning.
# URLs are https and versioned where the publisher has versions: schema.org
# release, git commit, OBO dated release, Wikidata entity revision. A row stays
# unversioned when the publisher offers only the current file (W3C /ns/, DCMI,
# Brick, QUDT 2.1, DBpedia live data, the GO and OBO "latest" files); its hash
# changes when the publisher edits it, and the warning is the signal.
